summary: Backend-only regression testing for LDC AI Platform. Wrote pytest suite (39 tests) covering auth, role-filtered cases, seeded capabilities/employees, launch/reopen, form submit+readonly lock (employee/manager/stakeholder/panel/hr), dashboard/status/audit, documents (upload/list/download/delete via Emergent object storage), and AI endpoints (write + 4 analyze types + latest). All 39 tests PASS against the external URL.

minor.issue: No explicit admin-only RBAC — any authenticated user can read full audit logs; consider restricting to admin/hr.

No role/ownership enforcement. Any authenticated user can PUT any role's form for any case. e.g. an employee token can save a manager-form or HR-review for any case. Readonly-after-submit is enforced, but submission authorship is not.
No 404 check if case_id does not exist — returns 200 with empty update. Should validate case existence.
Returns 200 {ok:true} even when doc_id does not exist (no 404). Also does not flip is_latest back to a previous version.
Does not validate employee_id exists; a bogus employee_id will create an orphan case.

action_items: Add RBAC to form PUT endpoints (employee-form → employee role + case ownership; manager-form → assigned manager; panel-review/mine → assigned panel member; hr-review → hr/hrbp; stakeholder-feedback/mine → stakeholder in manager.stakeholders list).
Validate case_id exists in launch/reopen/document-delete endpoints and return 404 when missing.
Validate employee_id exists on POST /api/cases and return 400/404 if not found.
critical_code_review_comments: routes_forms.py: form PUT handlers only rely on get_current_user without role/ownership checks. High-impact authorization gap — any authenticated user could save/submit any role's form content. Only readonly-after-submit is guarded.
routes_cases.py reopen endpoint: uses update_many with no filter on form identity; if a case had 2 panel reviews, it resets both — acceptable, but there is no existence check on case_id.
routes_documents.py delete is a soft-delete; it does not promote prior version to is_latest=True. If the latest doc is deleted, latest_by_type no longer contains it and no fallback exists.
core.get_object passes raw path into URL f-string — relies on path not containing special chars; UUID + safe chars so OK, but consider urllib.parse.quote for defensive coding.
routes_cases list_cases N+1: enriches each case with a separate employees.find_one call inside a loop. Fine at current scale (3 cases) but should batch-fetch for production.
test_credentials: Used seeded accounts from /app/memory/test_credentials.md — all 9 logins verified.
seed_data_creation: None. Used existing seed data (10 users, 3 employees, 8 capabilities, 3 cases). Tests prefix generated data with 'TEST_' where applicable. Test run does leave TEST_doc.txt uploads soft-deleted and mutates form contents on Alice case (reopened + re-submitted with TEST markers) — does not affect seed correctness but next iteration should be aware.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend fully green (39/39). All seeded login accounts, role-filtered GET /api/cases, form submit/readonly-lock for all 5 form types, admin-only create/launch/reopen, document upload→list→download(?auth=token)→delete via Emergent object storage, and Claude AI endpoints (/ai/write, /ai/analyze for 4 types, /ai/case/{id}/latest) confirmed working end-to-end. Main outstanding concern is authorization: form PUT endpoints accept any authenticated user. Also GET /api/audit is not role-restricted. If frontend testing is next, seeded Alice case has likely been reopened multiple times and employee-form/manager-form contents mutated by tests (contain 'TEST submitted'/'TEST' strings). Rerun seed_all or reset db if pristine state needed.
